user.title: Sugar Valley NeoPool Setup
user.description:
Welcome to the NeoPool integration setup.

**Important:** If you previously used the YAML package configuration, you **must** remove it from `configuration.yaml` and restart Home Assistant **before** proceeding.

If this is a fresh installation, simply confirm below and continue.

data.confirm_no_yaml: I confirm there is no active YAML package running

mqtt_confirm.title: NeoPool Device Discovered
mqtt_confirm.description: A NeoPool device was discovered on MQTT topic: **{device}**

yaml_migration.title: YAML Package Migration
yaml_migration.description:
Did you previously use the YAML package configuration and want to migrate your existing entities?

Migration will preserve all historical data (graphs, statistics) and entity customizations.

If this is a **fresh installation** with no previous YAML package, leave unchecked.

data.migrate_yaml: Yes, migrate my entities from the old YAML package

yaml_topic.title: MQTT Topic
yaml_topic.description:
Could not auto-detect your NeoPool device.

Please enter the MQTT topic configured in your Tasmota device.

yaml_no_entities.title: No YAML Entities Found
yaml_no_entities.description:
No existing YAML package entities were found in your Home Assistant instance.

If you used a custom `unique_id` prefix in your YAML package, check the box below to enter it manually.

Otherwise, leave unchecked to skip migration and set up your device as a fresh installation.

data.try_custom_prefix: I have a custom unique_id prefix to try

yaml_prefix.title: Custom Entity Prefix
yaml_prefix.description:
No entities found with the default prefix `neopool_mqtt_`.

If you customized the `unique_id` prefix in your YAML package, enter it below.

yaml_detect_confirm.title: Detected NeoPool Entities
yaml_detect_confirm.description:
We detected NeoPool YAML entities:

• **Unique ID prefix**: `{prefix}`
• **Entities found**: {entity_count}
• **Confidence**: {confidence}%

**Matched patterns**:
{matched_signatures}

---

If this is correct, check the box below to proceed.
If not, uncheck it to enter a custom prefix manually.

data.confirm_detection: Yes, this is correct - proceed with migration

yaml_active_warning.title: YAML Package Still Active
yaml_active_warning.description:
## ⚠️ Cannot Proceed - Entities Still Active

The following **{active_count}** entities are currently **receiving updates**, which means the YAML package is still running:

{entity_list}

---

## Required Actions:

1. **Remove or comment out** the YAML package from `configuration.yaml`
2. **Restart Home Assistant** completely
3. Come back to this screen and click **Retry**

---

⚠️ **Why is this required?**

If you proceed without removing the YAML package:
- You will get **duplicate entities** (both YAML and integration entities)
- Both sets will be active and receiving updates simultaneously
- This will cause confusion and require manual cleanup

The migration can only proceed once the YAML entities become **unavailable** (after removing the package and restarting).

yaml_confirm.title: Confirm Migration
yaml_confirm.description:
## Migration Summary

The following has been validated:

✓ **MQTT Topic**: `{topic}`
✓ **NodeID**: `{nodeid}`
✓ **Migratable entities found**: {entity_count}

### Entities to migrate:
{entity_list}

---

## What will happen:

1. Each entity's `unique_id` will be updated to include the NodeID
2. Entities will be associated with this integration
3. **All historical data will be preserved** (graphs, statistics)
4. Entity IDs will remain unchanged

---

⚠️ **Prerequisites** (confirm before proceeding):
- I have removed/commented out the YAML package from `configuration.yaml`
- I have restarted Home Assistant after removing the YAML package
- I understand this process will modify my entity registry

**This action cannot be undone automatically.** By checking the box below, you confirm you have completed the prerequisites and accept responsibility for this migration.

data.confirm_migration: I confirm I have completed the prerequisites and want to proceed

yaml_migration_result.title: Migration Complete

discover_device.title: Manual Setup

Enter your NeoPool device details.

For more information, see the [Tasmota NeoPool documentation]({docs_url}).

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure NeoPool
reconfigure.description:
Update your NeoPool device connection settings.

**Note:** Changing the device name will update the integration title. Check **Regenerate entity IDs** if you also want entity IDs to reflect the new name.

data_description.device_name: A friendly name for your pool controller
data_description.regenerate_entity_ids: Update entity IDs to match the new device name (e.g., sensor.neopool_ph → sensor.mypool_ph)
data_description.discovery_prefix: The MQTT topic used by your Tasmota device

error.cannot_connect: Could not receive messages from this MQTT topic. Verify the topic name and that your device is online. If the topic is correct, your device may publish telemetry infrequently — set 'TelePeriod 10' in the Tasmota console, then retry.

error.yaml_still_active: Entities are still active. Please remove the YAML package and restart Home Assistant first.

abort.not_neopool_device: The discovered device is not a NeoPool controller

abort.unique_id_mismatch: The device NodeID does not match the original configuration.

init.title: NeoPool Options
init.description:
Configure runtime options for your NeoPool device.

**Recovery Script Variables:**
When configured, the recovery script receives these variables:

- `device_name` : Device name
- `mqtt_topic` : MQTT topic
- `nodeid` : Device NodeID
- `failures_count` : Number of consecutive failures

data_description.recovery_script: Script to run when device is offline for too long
data_description.enable_repair_notification: Create a repair issue when device goes offline
data_description.failures_threshold: Number of consecutive LWT offline messages before triggering notifications
data_description.offline_timeout: How long the device must be offline before triggering notifications
data_description.connection_error_rate_threshold: Modbus error percentage (over a rolling 10-minute window) above which `binary_sensor.connection_problem` turns on
data_description.pump_type: Variable-speed pumps get per-timer speed controls. Auto-detect trusts the controller (variable-speed pumps report a speed); override only if needed.

device_offline.title: NeoPool device offline: {device_name}
device_offline.description:
The NeoPool device **{device_name}** has been offline for an extended period.

**MQTT Topic:** `{mqtt_topic}`

Please check:
- The Tasmota device is powered on
- The device is connected to your network
- The MQTT broker is running
- The MQTT topic is correct

set_timer.name: Set timer
set_timer.description: Configures one of the controller's built-in timers (filtration, light, or AUX). The schedule runs on the controller itself, independent of Home Assistant.

start.name: Start
start.description: Time of day the relay turns on.

stop.name: Stop
stop.description: Time of day the relay turns off (the run duration is derived from start and stop).

period.name: Repeat period
period.description: How often the timer repeats, in seconds (86400 = every day).

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Timer working mode: Auto runs the schedule, On forces the relay on, Off forces it off, Disabled turns the timer off.

set_timer_unknown_device.message: No NeoPool controller found for device {device_id}.
